sn45.8:3.3: For further explanation of right view, see MN 2, MN 117, SN 12:15, and AN 10:93.
sn45.8:5.3: For more on right speech, see MN 58, SN 11:5, AN 4:183, AN 5:198, AN 10:176, and Sn 3:3.
sn45.8:6.2: DN 22 and MN 141, when analyzing right action, replace “abstaining from sexual intercourse” with “abstaining from sexual misconduct.”
sn45.8:8.6: For more on right effort, see MN 101 and AN 6:55.
sn45.8:9.6: For further explanation of right mindfulness, see DN 22 and the book, Right Mindfulness.
sn45.8:10.2: For the meaning of “sensuality,” here, see AN 6:63. “And what, monks, are unskillful qualities? Wrong view, wrong resolve, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration.” — SN 45:22
sn45.8:10.6: For further explanation of right concentration, see MN 44, MN 111, AN 4:41, AN 5:28, and AN 9:36. MN 44 explains why pain is not abandoned until pleasure is abandoned on entering the fourth jhāna: [Visākha:] “In what way is pleasant feeling pleasant, lady, and in what way painful?” [Sister Dhammadinnā:] “Pleasant feeling is pleasant in remaining, & painful in changing, friend Visākha. Painful feeling is painful in remaining & pleasant in changing. Neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling is pleasant in occurring together with knowledge, and painful in occurring without knowledge.”
